title: What simulated live is
summary: Same Operator as backtest, but the clock is real time (mode=0). Ask explains only; it does not start Trader.
narrative:
Simulated live uses the same Operator and strategy logic as a backtest. The difference is the clock and who matches orders: backtest fast-forwards a historical window; simulated live advances on the real trading calendar (configure mode=0). Matching is usually a simulator Broker, not a real exchange desk yet.

Roles to name only: Operator holds the strategies; Trader is the process that runs them on a schedule; Broker accepts orders and returns fills. Broker setup, startup recipes, risk checklists, and troubleshooting commands stay in the live-trading manual. This card does not list them.

Ask explains this boundary. It does not start Trader and does not submit orders.

The number below names the next window. A later question may refer to a number; explain that item from its card.

1. Live-trade steps are never sent automatically. Ask does not start Trader, and a plan does not become an order by itself.
